messages:
maya_support: Hey team — just got flagged by AcctResp: customer ACMECorp keeps getting 403 with body '{"error":"forbidden","reason":"insufficient_entitlement"}' when calling /v1/generate. They say their API key is the same one that was working yesterday.

maya_support: Repro steps from customer: curl with Authorization: Bearer <key> -> 403. Customer is on 'growth' plan, trying to access model 'redwood-xlarge-enterprise'. They expect graceful downgrade but are getting hard 403.

alex_lee: Thanks Maya. Can you paste the raw response headers and the curl command they used? Also, any recent billing changes for that account?

maya_support: Pasted from customer:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc123" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-xlarge-enterprise","input":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2025 18:32:10 GMT
x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d4e

{"error":"forbidden","reason":"insufficient_entitlement","detail":"model_not_in_plan"}
```

maya_support: Account metadata: plan=growth, billing_status=active, seats=12, region=us-west-2. No recent plan change per billing UI.

sanjay_ops: @maya_support I'm going to trace the request through the auth proxy logs. Can you give me the x-request-id?

maya_support: x-request-id is 0a1b2c3d4e (in message above).

opsbot: Incident INC-2025-378 created for account ACMECorp referencing 0a1b2c3d4e — severity: high — assigned: sanjay_ops.

sanjay_ops: I pulled the auth-proxy trace. It hits entitlement-service.v2 -> returns 403 with code ENT_403. The entitlement check looked up plan 'growth' and checked model allowlist; growth does NOT include redwood-xlarge-enterprise (that's enterprise-only). BUT I'm seeing an odd mapping: the model alias mapping service returned 'redwood-xlarge-enterprise' mapped to capability flag 'enterprise_vector_opt' and that flag is incorrectly marked enabled for growth in the feature-flag cache.

julia_engineer: That feature-flag cache is populated from FF-Config service via Kafka. There was a config push last night (PR #4321) that added a temporary flag to enable 'enterprise_vector_opt' for partners during a trial. Could ACME have been backfilled?

maya_support: Customer insists they never got a trial. Billing shows active growth plan, no trial.

alex_lee: Two hypotheses: 1) entitlement-service mis-evaluated plan vs flag precedence, or 2) the UI/DB says growth but service read a stale plan id (race during migration). Which logs do we have?

sanjay_ops: Checked DB read: account.plan_id=growth (read at 2025-06-09T18:31:59Z). Entitlement decision logs:
```
ent_decision: account=acct_98765 plan=growth model_alias=redwood-xlarge-enterprise feature_flag=enterprise_vector_opt flag_value=true source=ffcache ttl_remaining=120s
ent_result: deny -> insufficient_entitlement (model_not_in_plan)
```
Strange: ffcache says flag true which would usually allow but entitlement engine still denied — looks like flag shouldn't be considered higher precedence than plan allowlist. There's a precedence bug.

julia_engineer: Confirmed — recent change in entitlement-engine (release 2025-06-05, commit 9f8a) unintentionally changed precedence: feature flags were evaluated before plan allowlists and could override them. That explains inconsistency across accounts. PR rolling back that part is at https://git.redwood/infra/entitlement-engine/pulls/4387.

charles_cs: Customer impact: some growth accounts might get allowed on enterprise models intermittently (if flag is true), while most still get 403. Very confusing for customers and support.

billing_bot: Note: billing notifications show no invoices failed for acct_98765. Billing tenant status: active. No trial tags.

alex_lee: Action plan: 1) rollback entitlement-engine change (PR 4387) to restore plan precedence, 2) invalidate FF cache entries for enterprise_vector_opt across all regions to remove inconsistent true values, 3) run a quicksearch for accounts that got temporary access and add to a list for CS outreach, 4) send an interim customer-facing note explaining we identified a gating bug and are rolling a fix.

sanjay_ops: I'm on the rollback. Spun up canary with reverted behavior to internal canary cluster. Canary logs show requests for ACMECorp now return 402? Wait odd.

maya_support: 402? That would be payment required. Did anything else change?

sanjay_ops: Looks like the entitlement engine returned 'fallback:needs_upgrade' which maps to 402 in the API layer. I think the mapping table between entitlement codes and HTTP codes was tweaked in the same release. Will revert mapping as well.

julia_engineer: Yup the same release touched both precedence and mapping. I'll land hotfix for mapping and then merge rollback for precedence. Deploy sequence: mapping hotfix -> invalidate cache -> merge precedence rollback -> full deploy.

opsbot: Canary deploy of entitlement-engine@hotfix-mapping succeeded (canary-1/3).

sanjay_ops: Cache invalidation script ran:
```
# invalidate ffcache key enterprise_vector_opt
for r in us-west-2 us-east-1 eu-west-1; do
  curl -X POST "https://ffcache.$r.internal/invalidate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -d '{"keys":["enterprise_vector_opt"]}'
done
```

sanjay_ops: After invalidation and mapping hotfix, I retried the original curl from support but with a staging API key: got 403 with reason 'insufficient_entitlement' (expected). Replaced model with 'redwood-xlarge' (allowed) -> 200 OK.

maya_support: I asked ACME to retry. They replied: "We retried and now get 403 -> trying smaller model works, thanks. We had a demo yesterday where it unexpectedly worked — was super confusing."

charles_cs: Let's prepare a short blurb for the customer: apology, root cause (entitlement precedence bug + cached ff value), what we did (reverted, invalidated cache), what we are doing next (scan & outreach), ETA for outreach. I'll draft and post here.

alex_lee: Also add internal follow-ups: postmortem, add unit tests to ensure plan allowlist precedence, add an alert for sudden spike in ENT_403 followed by ENT_allowed events for same account, and make feature flag TTL shorter for model gating flags.

maya_support: Customer blurb draft: "Hi ACME — we found a bug where temporary feature flags could momentarily override plan protections and cause inconsistent access behavior. We've reverted the change, cleared caches, and verified your access now behaves consistently (enterprise models remain restricted on Growth plan). We're sorry for the confusion; a CS rep will reach out to go over impacted requests and offer assistance." Thoughts?

charles_cs: Good. Add: "If you believe you should have access to enterprise models, we'll fast-track a trial or upgrade conversation."

julia_engineer: Quick note for ops: we'll run a backfill scan to find accounts that were granted enterprise access between 2025-06-05T00:00:00Z and 2025-06-09T19:00:00Z. I'll export results to S3 and tag accounts for CS.

sanjay_ops: Backfill started (job id backfill-20250609-1). Estimated runtime ~4h, will post results.

opsbot: Deploy full rollout of entitlement-engine@v2.14.8 (post-hotfix) scheduled in 30m.

alex_lee: Thanks all. Maya/Charles, please coordinate outreach and mark affected accounts as 'investigating' in the support tracker. Sanjay/Julia: ensure we have logs and PR references for postmortem. Close the ticket once outreach initiated.

maya_support: Will do. Tagging CS ticket TKT-5562 for ACMECorp. I'll attach logs and the curl repro.

charles_cs: I'll own the customer email + check with account team.

maya_support: Customer replied: :thumbsup: "Thanks — that explains the flakiness. Happy to coordinate for logs if needed."

sanjay_ops: Update: backfill completed. Found 27 accounts with temporary enterprise allowlist flag true; 6 of them executed generate calls to enterprise models during window. CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-reports/backfills/entitlement-backfill-20250609.csv.

julia_engineer: Filing postmortem draft and linking PRs: https://git.redwood/infra/entitlement-engine/pulls/4387 (rollback) and https://git.redwood/infra/entitlement-engine/pulls/4391 (mapping hotfix).

alex_lee: Good job everyone. We'll keep this thread open until CS outreach confirmed. Closing notes: add unit test for precedence and revert feature flag TTL change in next sprint.

maya_support: Closing support ticket as "root cause identified & mitigated; CS outreach in progress" — will reopen if ACME reports issues.
